title.narrative: Provision of life-saving WASH assistance to the most severely drought affected communities in Xudur district, Bakool region, Somalia

description.narrative: ltpgtAction Against Hunger proposes an eight‑month emergency WASH response for the drought hit Xudur district in Bakool, Somalia. The intervention will support the HRP goals of preventing loss of life (SO1) and sustaining livelihoods (SO2) and will aim to restore safe water, sanitation and hygiene for 14,500 individuals, including boys (2,938), girls (3,227), men (4,021), and women (4,314).ltbrgtACF will provide safe water through a 30 day water trucking operation that will deliver 1,215,000 Lof chlorinated water (7.5 L person⁻¹ day⁻¹) to 5,400 beneficiaries in IDP camps. Each household will receive a hygiene kit containing a 20 L container, two 2 L jerrycans, soap and a household‑water‑treatment kit. Twelve water‑quality checks (chlorine ≥ 0.2 mg/L, turbidity ≤ 5 NTU, E. coli = 0) will be carried out community water monitors will be trained to continue testing after the trucking phase using a low cost field kit and SOP.ltbrgtTo ensure longer‑term access, ACF will also rehabilitate one existing borehole (Gabiney) and four shallow wells (Bullow, Madawarabe, Amari) with Afridev hand‑pumps delivering about 1 080 L per hour. A 3 km pipeline will extend water from Gabiney to four communal kiosks equipped with tap‑stands, handwashing stations and solar lighting. A water point chlorination campaign will target 50 water points using calcium hypochlorite (HTH 65 %). Thirty‑Four water‑committee members (22 M, 12 F) will receive three‑day training on operation, OM, financial management and cost‑recovery.ltbrgtSanitation will include 28 gender‑segregated emergency latrines (840 users) with lockable doors, iron‑sheet superstructures, handwashing stations and solar lighting ten of these will be disability‑friendly (ramps, handrails). ACF will distribute 40 sanitation tool kits to community groups, accompanied by training on safe handling and waste segregation. It will also organise ten community led clean‑up campaigns across IDP sites and vulnerable settlements, using gender sensitive IEC materials to promote solid‑waste management and reduce vector‑borne disease.lt/pgtltpgtHygiene promotion will be led by 18 Community Hygiene Promoters (12 F, 6 M) who will be trained in a three‑day programme covering hygiene techniques, gender equality and disability inclusion. Each promoter will serve about seven household visits per week (28 per month) to deliver behaviour change messages on hand‑washing, safe food preparation, protected water chains and household water treatment. Additionally, ACF will distribute 900 hygiene kits (soap, jerrycans, bucket, water purification tablets, sanitary wear) with hands‑on demonstrations.ltbrgtThe exit strategy will centre on community ownership: water committees will map long term solutions, coordinate borehole rehabilitation and establish cost recovery mechanisms trained committees, SOPs and low cost kits will enable continued water‑quality monitoring. Sanitation facilities will be handed over to local caretakers with a clear maintenance plan, and hygiene promoters will transition to a community‑led model supported by health and nutrition facilities. ACF will embed gender equality, protection mainstreaming and disability inclusion throughout the project, ensuring at least 30% female representation in decision making bodies, providing GBV sensitive training for promoters and constructing ten disability friendly latrines.ltbrgtlt/pgt
